# S81 — Add a reusable multi-field text input to the TUI

The TUI only has single-line, single-purpose prompts (search, jump, move). The
interactive roadmap wizard needs to collect several free-text fields in
sequence. That input widget should exist once, as a reusable primitive, before
the wizard is built on it.

**Findings:** v1.0.0 readiness audit; prerequisite for the roadmap wizard (S50) · **Size:** M · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-09-27** — Delivered as the wizard's text_input primitive (tui_wizard.py), reused by the TUI search/jump/move prompts.

**Not in this slice:** the wizard flow itself (S50 consumes this), and any
mouse/drag interaction.

## Why

Building the wizard directly would either duplicate prompt handling or grow it
ad hoc. A tested, reusable multi-field text input keeps the wizard thin and keeps
every decision in a pure, terminal-free function as the TUI's design requires.

## Files

- `src/slicer/tui.py` — a new prompt/mode primitive alongside `_prompt`/`_move`
- `tests/test_tui.py`

## Failing tests

1. Typing, backspace, cursor/field advance, submit, and cancel are all decided
   by pure functions driven through `View.handle`, no terminal.
2. Multi-field entry collects each field and yields the full result on submit;
   cancel discards it.

## Implement

Generalize the existing prompt pattern into a reusable text-input mode that
supports full-line editing (not just append) and stepping through an ordered set
of labeled fields, returning the collected values to the caller. Keep all logic
in `act`/`View` methods testable without curses, mirroring `_prompt`/`_move`, and
render its state through the one `draw` surface.

## Check

The primitive drives a multi-field entry end to end in tests without a terminal;
existing prompt modes are unaffected.
